title: Much / Many / A few / A little

leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Much / Many / A few / A little
leadIn.content: Asking about quantities: How many books do you have? How much sugar do you want in your tea?

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Much / Many / A few / A little?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of Much / Many / A few / A little require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: Much / Many / A few / A little
form.content: Countable: How many / many / a few + plural noun. Uncountable: How much / much / a little + uncountable noun.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Much / Many / A few / A little
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Much / Many / A few / A little.

controlledPractice.question: 'There is ___ milk left.' (a small uncountable amount)
controlledPractice.explanation: A little is used for small uncountable quantities.

controlledPractice.question: Most natural in an affirmative sentence:
options: I have a lot of water.
controlledPractice.explanation: 'A lot of' is the natural choice in affirmative sentences; 'much' suits questions/negatives.
